source: BCCSA COR® OHS Audit Tool V2 — R13 (Jan 1, 2026)

questions.text: Is signed by the president, CEO or local senior management?
Includes management's commitment to provide a safe and healthy work environment?
Recognizes the right of workers to work in a safe and healthy work environment?
Is current and dated?
Is reviewed annually by management?
Is prominently posted or made available to the worker?
Addresses accountability and responsibility for health and safety for all workplace parties?
Expresses a commitment to work in a spirit of consultation and cooperation with the workers?
Is understood by personnel?
Are written hazard assessments conducted as required?
Does the employer use an ongoing hazard assessment process?
Are appropriate personnel involved in the hazard assessment process?
Are the hazards identified?
Are the hazards prioritized?
Is there a list of identified critical tasks?
Are controls developed for identified hazards?
Are controls implemented in a timely manner?
Are appropriate personnel involved in or informed of the control strategies?
Does the company have a process for evaluating and monitoring subcontractors?
Does management support the ongoing application of the hazard assessment process?
Do the safe work practices accurately reflect the company's activities?
Have applicable safe work practices been written?
Are they understood by workers?
Are they readily available?
Are they followed by workers on a regular basis?
Have both management/supervisors and workers participated in the development and/or review of safe work practices?
Do the safe job procedures accurately reflect the employer's activities?
Have all critical safe job procedures been written?
Are they understood by workers?
Are safe job procedures followed on a regular basis?
Are these procedures available and easily accessible to workers?
Have both management/supervisors and workers participated in the development and/or review of these procedures?
Are the rules clearly stated in writing?
Are the rules prominently posted or provided to each worker?
Do workers understand company and site specific rules?
Does the program address non-conformance and progressive disciplinary actions?
Are the rules applied and enforced consistently with all employees?
Is there a written policy for PPE?
Are workers made aware of the requirements for PPE?
Do all employees have access to basic PPE?
Is specialized PPE available to workers when required?
Is the correct PPE used by all employees when required?
Are there written procedures for the proper fitting, care and use of specialized PPE?
Are employees given instruction or training in the use of PPE as required?
Are there criteria used to select PPE?
Is there a system in place to regularly inspect and maintain basic and specialized PPE?
An inventory of items to be maintained?
Maintenance meeting regulatory and manufacturers' standards?
The use and completion of schedules and checklists as required?
Records with a description of corrective actions taken?
Is there a system to effectively remove defective tools, equipment and vehicles from service?
Is this system followed?
Does a qualified and competent person perform the inspections and maintenance?
Does the employer have a formal orientation program?
Is orientation mandatory for all new employees before starting work?
Is there a standardized written orientation form?
Does the form provide for signatures of workers and the person conducting the orientation?
Are mandatory training requirements verified or training provided before starting work?
Are training records maintained?
Is job specific training provided and documented as required?
Does a competent person conduct job specific training?
Have supervisors received training in workplace inspections and health and safety responsibilities?
Is a system in place to measure knowledge and competency?
Does the employer hold scheduled health and safety meetings?
Does senior management attend and participate in health and safety meetings?
Is a prepared agenda followed and are minutes and attendance of the meeting kept?
Does two-way communication exist during these meetings?
Are tailgate or toolbox meetings held regularly and documented as per policy?
Is there a written policy for inspections?
Does the policy include frequency of inspections?
Is the required frequency being met?
Is there a form or checklist used for inspections?
Are supervisors performing inspections as required?
Are workers involved in the inspection process?
Are all areas inspected as required?
Are identified deficiencies corrected in a timely manner?
Does senior management review or participate in the inspection process?
Are inspection reports posted or communicated to appropriate employees?
Is there a written investigation policy and reporting procedure?
Is the policy being followed?
Are standardized forms readily available and used?
Do workers know the reporting process?
Have supervisors been trained in investigation and reporting procedures?
Are appropriate employees involved in investigations?
Are no-loss incidents (close calls) being reported?
Are recommendations for prevention or remedial action implemented in a timely manner?
Are corrective actions communicated to workers?
Are investigation reports reviewed by management?
Are the emergency preparedness plans appropriate to work activities?
Does the plan include a requirement for training in emergency procedures, roles,  and responsibilities?
Has the emergency response plan been tested for deficiencies and corrective action taken?
Does the employer have a written fire response plan?
Are the correct class and size of extinguishers available, marked, and visible?
Are extinguishers regularly inspected and maintained?
Is an appropriate emergency communication system available?
Are there adequate first aid supplies and facilities?
Are the required number of qualified first aid personnel on-site?
Is there a means to transport an injured employee to a medical facility?
Is there a process to organize and manage program documentation?
Are adequate health and safety activity summaries developed and maintained?
Are health and safety statistical reports generated on an ongoing basis and readily available?
Does the company compare health and safety performance year to year?
Are the annual statistics analyzed and needs or trends identified?
Are adequate first aid treatment records kept?
Was an action plan developed based on the most recent audit?
Was an action plan communicated and implemented?
Are copies of relevant legislation posted or available at each workplace?
Does management/supervision regularly refer to relevant legislation during job planning?
Are employees aware of their rights and responsibilities and how to exercise them?
Does the employer's injury and incident reporting meet the legislated requirement?

elements.title: Joint Health and Safety Committee or Worker Representative

questions.text: Is there communication between the employees and worker health and safety representative(s)?
Has a Terms of Reference (TOR) been established for the JOHS Committee or Worker Representative(s)?
Have committee members or worker representative(s) received training to carry out their duties, functions, and responsibilities?
Are committee members or the worker representative(s) following the duties outlined in the Terms of Reference?
Are members of the JOHS Committee or Worker Representative(s) involved in inspections, incident investigations, or the resolution of safety issues?
